records.summary: 414 Columbus Ave is in the North Beach NCD where restaurants are conditional uses on the first story and may only be approved in spaces last legally occupied by a restaurant or bar. The records show this address has operated as "Original U.S. Restaurant" continuously since at least 1986, with an active Type 41 license since 2016 and three prior CUAs (1986, 1998, 2010) that added entertainment and upgraded the license from Type 41 to Type 47. The 1987 CUA (Case No. 1986.553C) specifically approved replacing the beer & wine license with a full liquor license "with no change in operation, furniture fixtures, or building." Within 500 feet there are 60 registered food and drink businesses including 12 bars, 40 active on-sale ABC licenses, and 97 total on-sale licenses within 1,000 feet—flagging possible undue concentration. The block has approved numerous restaurant continuations and license upgrades; five dated use decisions in the last five years were all approved, though the sample is too small for a rate.

patterns.pattern: Once a Type 47 license is approved for a restaurant via CUA, subsequent transfers and renewals of that license are handled by Planning as routine agency referrals (Miscellaneous Permits) rather than new CUAs. Multiple agency referrals show Planning recommending approval for Type 47 continuation based on prior CUA authorization and compliance with Sections 722 and 780.3.

The 2020 amendments to Planning Code Sections 722 and 780.3 (Ordinance 182-20, effective November 2020) allowed certain limited restaurants in North Beach to convert to full restaurants and obtain Type 41 licenses without CUA or 311 notice, provided they had operated as bona fide eating places for at least three full calendar years. Post-2020 agency referrals cite this ordinance and approve resta…

Planning consistently approves restaurant use continuations and alcohol license transfers in North Beach when the space was last legally occupied by a restaurant or limited restaurant and the use has not been abandoned. Multiple agency referrals approved continuation of existing restaurant uses without Section 312 notice when there is no change of use or expansion.

Type 47 licenses for restaurants are repeatedly described by Planning as 'permitted in conjunction with a Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place' under Sections 722 and 780.3. The key criterion is that the establishment must operate and maintain the licensed premises as a bona fide eating place, meaning meal service is primary and alcohol service is incidental.

No extracted conditions appear in any of the approved Type 47 agency referrals or recent Type 41 agency referrals, suggesting that when the restaurant use is continuing and the applicant commits to maintaining a bona fide eating place, Planning approves the license continuation or transfer without additional operating restrictions beyond the underlying zoning and ABC requirements.

Agency referrals that cite prior CUA authorization (e.g. citing a CPC Motion number or prior case number) are routinely approved by Planning for continuation of the authorized use. The prior CUA establishes the use as legally permitted, and subsequent transfers, renewals, and health/ABC referrals are handled administratively.

overall.next_step: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning (entitlement path requires CUA, ABC Type 47 transfer, and health permit); begin the CUA process before or in parallel with ABC license escrow and make the lease contingent on CUA approval.

approvals.summary: Upgrading from Type 41 to Type 47 at an existing restaurant in North Beach is intensification of a conditional use and requires a new Conditional Use Authorization under Planning Code § 178 and § 780.3(c)(2)(A), with a Planning Commission hearing and 30-day appeal period.

findings.text: An active Type 41 beer-and-wine license (ABC #564474) has been on file at 414 Columbus Avenue since March 2016, and the space has continuously operated as Original U.S. Restaurant since at least 1986.

Planning Commission Motion No. 13556 (Case No. 1986.553C, approved February 1987) authorized replacing the existing Type 41 license with Type 47 at this address 'with no change in operation, furniture fixtures, or building.'

North Beach NCD § 780.3(c)(1)(B) (in force on March 9, 2022, repealed December 15, 2025) required Conditional Use Authorization for a restaurant that stays the same use but is intensified; adding spirits service is intensification.

Nine comparable agency referrals approved between 2017 and 2021 within 105 meters show that once a Type 47 license is authorized via CUA, Planning approves subsequent transfers and renewals administratively as agency referrals (Miscellaneous Permits) when the restaurant use continues with no expansion.

The description does not state whether Mona Lisa Mare e Monti is part of a chain, so formula retail (which is not permitted in North Beach NCD per § 722) is not decided. The description also does not state whether the proposal changes conditions of the 1987, 1998, or 2010 CUA approvals on file.

approvals.summary: The Type 47 license transfer requires ABC investigation and posting, and ABC will review undue concentration because census tract 106.00 shows 52 active on-sale licenses against 12 authorized; a public convenience or necessity finding is likely required from the city before ABC will issue the licen…

findings.text: Census tract 106.00 shows 52 active on-sale retail licenses as of March 9, 2022, against 12 authorized under ABC's September 2026 census tract authorizations, triggering an undue-concentration review under Business and Professions Code § 23958.4.

When a census tract is over the authorized number of licenses, state law tests a premises-to-premises transfer for undue concentration; the license may still issue if public convenience or necessity would be served.

ABC referral approvals at 431 Columbus (2017), 1512 Stockton (2019), and 411 Columbus (2021) show that ABC issued Type 47 and Type 41 licenses in this census tract for bona fide eating places, though the records do not show whether a PCN finding was required in those cases.

The 1987 CUA at this address required the restaurant to maintain bona fide eating place status, which North Beach SUD § 780.3(c)(2)(A) (in force on March 9, 2022) defined as at least 51% of gross receipts from food prepared and sold on the premises.

approvals.summary: The health permit to operate is issued after plan check and inspection without a hearing; the existing restaurant has a current health permit and no construction is proposed, so renewal or transfer under the new entity is allowed as of right.

findings.text: Agency referrals at 411 Columbus (2021), 658 Vallejo (2021), and 431 Columbus (2018) show that DPH referrals for continuation of existing restaurant use with no expansion are approved by Planning within 10 to 22 days with no conditions.
A certified food safety manager and food handler cards for all employees are required before DPH issues the permit to operate, per California Retail Food Code §§ 113947.1 and 113948.

approvals.summary: The rules cannot establish whether a building permit is needed because the description does not state the occupant load (whether the space is for fewer than 50 people) and the existing occupancy group is not in public records; only plans or an inspection show that.

findings.text: The concept states no tenant improvements, no new construction, and no exterior signage, and the existing use is restaurant, so if the occupancy group does not change, no building permit with plan review is needed.

2019 California Building Code § 303.1.1 and § 303.3 classify a restaurant or bar with 50 or more occupants as Assembly Group A-2 and a space for fewer than 50 people as Group B; the description gives no occupant load.

If the space is A-2 now and remains A-2, or is B and remains B, there is no change of occupancy under the Building Code. If the occupant load or the assembly character changes, a building permit with DBI, Fire, and Planning routing may be required.

expected_conditions.condition: The restaurant must operate and maintain the licensed premises as a bona fide eating place, with at least 51% of gross receipts from food prepared and sold to guests on the premises.
expected_conditions.basis: North Beach SUD § 780.3(c)(2)(A) (in force on March 9, 2022) required restaurants with on-sale liquor licenses to maintain bona fide eating place status and to provide the Department with gross receipts records on request. Nine agency referrals between 2017 and 2021 repeatedly state 'Must operate and maintain the licensed premises as a bona fide eating place' as a condition of Type 41 and Type 47 approval.

expected_conditions.condition: The use may not be significantly altered, enlarged, or intensified beyond the scope of the CUA authorization without a new Conditional Use.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 178 (in force since before 2022-01-01) prohibits significant alteration, enlargement, or intensification of a conditional use without a new CUA. The 1987 CUA at this address approved the Type 47 license 'with no change in operation, furniture fixtures, or building,' and subsequent approvals for restaurant continuations in North Beach repeatedly cite § 178 to limit expansion.

expected_conditions.condition: Hours of alcohol service until 2 a.m., consistent with the existing Type 41 license and North Beach NCD hours (principally permitted 6 a.m. to 2 a.m.).
expected_conditions.basis: North Beach NCD § 722 (in force on March 9, 2022) set principally permitted hours of 6 a.m. to 2 a.m. and not permitted hours of 2 a.m. to 6 a.m. The description states the restaurant does not close after midnight and does not close after 2 a.m., so the existing hours are within the principally permitted window. No comparable CUA in the record set restricted hours below 2 a.m. for restaurants with Type 47.

expected_conditions.condition: Compliance with ABC license Type 47 requirements: food must be available during all hours of alcohol service, and minors are allowed when accompanied by a parent or guardian.
expected_conditions.basis: ABC Type 47 (on-sale general, eating place) is a bona fide eating place license under Business and Professions Code § 23038; food service is required during all hours of alcohol service. The catalog entry and ABC regulations impose this requirement statewide.

filing_playbook.action: Secure the entity formation, EIN, seller's permit, and San Francisco business registration certificate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation), obtain the federal EIN online from the IRS, register for the California seller's permit with CDTFA, and file for the San Francisco business registration certificate with the Treasurer & Tax Collector. ABC will not process the license transfer until the entity, EIN, seller's permit, and lease are in place. The business registration certificate generates the Business Account Number (BAN) that every other city department requires.

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning Department, requesting authorization to intensify the existing restaurant use by upgrading from Type 41 to Type 47 on-sale general license.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Frame the application as intensification of an existing legally permitted restaurant use under Planning Code § 178, citing the 1987 CUA (Motion No. 13556, Case No. 1986.553C) that previously authorized a Type 47 license at this address. Emphasize that the restaurant has operated continuously since 1986 with no interruption or abandonment, that the space will not be enlarged, that no construction or change of use is proposed, and that the applicant will maintain the restaurant as a bona fide eating place with at least 51% of gross receipts from food sales. Submit a business plan showing that meal service is primary and alcohol service is incidental. Pre-application meeting with the Planning staff is recommended to confirm the scope and to determine whether the 1987, 1998, and 2010 CUA conditions will carry forward or be superseded.

filing_playbook.action: Identify and enter escrow for a Type 47 license through a California ABC license broker, with the purchase agreement contingent on CUA approval and ABC transfer approval.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Type 47 is a quota license; new licenses are not issued by ABC in San Francisco County, so the license must be purchased on the open market and transferred to the premises. Engage an ABC license broker to locate an available Type 47 license (expect $100,000 to $450,000 in San Francisco). The escrow period is typically 90 to 180 days. Make the lease and the license purchase contingent on Planning's CUA approval and ABC's transfer approval, including any public convenience or necessity finding required for the undue-concentration census tract.

filing_playbook.action: File the ABC Type 47 premises-to-premises transfer application with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control after the CUA is approved or in parallel if the CUA hearing date is confirmed.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the ABC-257 transfer application, the signed lease, a copy of the entity formation documents, the seller's permit, a diagram of the premises, and the transfer fee. ABC will investigate the applicant, post a 30-day public notice at the premises, and refer the application to SFPD and San Francisco Planning for review. Planning will issue a zoning sign-off only after the CUA is granted. Prepare a written statement for ABC explaining that the restaurant has operated continuously as a bona fide eating place since 1986 and that the Type 47 license will be used solely in conjunction with meal service. Because census tract 106.00 is over the authorized number of on-sale licenses, ABC may require a public convenience or necessity finding from the city; coordinate with Planning and the Board of Supervisors early if ABC requests one.

filing_playbook.action: Complete RBS (Responsible Beverage Service) training for all alcohol servers and managers and obtain food handler cards and a food safety manager certificate for the staff.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Every alcohol server and manager must complete ABC-approved RBS training within 60 days of hire (AB 1221); register on the ABC RBS Portal and complete an approved course. Every employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of hire, and the restaurant must have at least one certified food protection manager on staff before DPH issues the permit to operate. Schedule these certifications before the ABC transfer is approved so staff are ready when the license is issued.

filing_playbook.action: Renew or transfer the health permit to operate with San Francisco Department of Public Health under the new entity after the CUA is granted.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: If the ownership or entity type is changing, file for a new health permit to operate; if only the license type is changing, coordinate with DPH to update the permit. The existing restaurant already has a health permit on file, and no construction is proposed, so DPH should treat this as a continuation of the existing use. Submit the BAN, the certified food safety manager certificate, proof of workers' compensation insurance, and the menu. DPH may require a pre-opening inspection if the entity or operator is new; schedule this inspection at least two weeks in advance.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses for recorded music before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Federal copyright law requires a blanket performance license to play music publicly, whether recorded or live. Apply online to ASCAP and BMI for annual licenses (formula-based fees, typically $300 to $2,500 each for a restaurant of this size). The licenses are effective immediately upon approval and are separate from the city and state permits.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline of 120 to 300 days and cost of $3,100 to $465,000 are for approvals granted: the Conditional Use Authorization (120 to 300 days from filing to approval, $3,100 to $15,000 depending on construction cost, per the catalog and comparable CUA filings in North Beach), the ABC Type 47 premises-to-premises transfer (90 to 240 days including escrow, posting, ABC investigation, and city referrals; $17,000 to $450,000 for the license purchase on the open market plus $1,000 to $1,600 in ABC fees), and the health permit to operate (14 to 45 days, $470 to $1,000). The CUA is the critical path: comparable CUA filings at 1318 Grant (2015-000635CUA) took 159 days from filing to approval. ABC transfer timelines depend on undue-concentration review; if ABC requires a public convenience or necessity finding from the Board of Supervisors, add 60 to 120 days to the ABC timeline. The cost range reflects the Type 47 license purchase price, which dominates the total; the applicant should confirm current market prices through an ABC broker before committing to the lease. These figures do not include denial or withdrawal; the nine comparable approvals in the precedent set took 9 to 159 days, all approved. Business registration, entity formation, seller's permit, RBS training, food handler cards, food safety manager certification, and music licenses add 1 to 35 days and $635 to $3,385 in fees, but those are not entitlement approvals and are handled in parallel.
